text: CONTRADICTING: Acidic organelles (lysosomal-related) in immortalized APOE4 astrocytes were slightly but significantly more alkaline (higher pH, by 0.14 units) than in APOE3 astrocytes, rather than more acidic (reported: 0.14 pH units).
description: Immortalized astrocytes derived from human APOE3- and APOE4-targeted-replacement mice (gift of D. Holtzman; Morikawa et al. 2005), grown in advanced DMEM with 10% FBS, passages up to 10. Cells were loaded with 2 μM LysoSensor Yellow/Blue DND-160, and a pH calibration curve (pH 4.0-6.0, monensin/nigericin) was run for each condition. Readout was 340/390 nm excitation ratio on a fluorometer. N = 3, presumably independent experiments/passages. Caveat: mouse immortalized (aneuploid) astrocytes, not human brain astrocytes. The probe reports the pH of the bulk acidic-organelle population (mostly lysosomes), not endosomes specifically. The authors note that compartment-specific endosomal pH differences may exist.

provenance.excerpt: We found that both APOE3 and APOE4 astrocytes had standard lysosomal-related pH, with a minimal but significant difference of 0.14 pH units between genotypes, APOE4 lysosomes being more alkaline (Fig. 4g).

meccogFinding.summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher pH of lysosome-enriched acidic organelles in immortalized mouse astrocytes) [CONTRADICTS]

warnings: effect size '0.14 pH units' has no accepted form: recorded as qualitative, numbers kept in description

perturbed.variable: APOE4 vs APOE3 genotype (immortalized astrocytes from human APOE targeted-replacement mice)

measured.variable: luminal pH of acidic organelles (lysosome-enriched), measured with LysoSensor Yellow/Blue ratiometric fluorometry
